description: maintenance-verbs M1, D0.3-ratified deferred-completion shape. Dispatches a rotate_session choreography job (resolve the ledger row, durable role-inbox pickup dispatch, clear_session, drive_session, then verify a new claude_session_id was actually observed) and returns {job_id, status: 'queued'} in milliseconds — the choreography itself runs in a background worker, never inline in this call. Poll check_choreography_job_status with the returned job_id for the outcome; this verb never blocks for the rotation to finish.
embedding_description: Free up a healthy but context-full session's window with a fresh /clear and a driven pickup turn, keeping the SAME live process and role binding the whole time — the routine context-hygiene operation for a session that is fine, just full, never for a dead or unresponsive one (that is restart_session's job).

result_processor_customizations.result_description: {job_id, status: 'queued'} — the dispatch's own outcome, NOT the rotation's outcome.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: State plainly that this only confirms the job was queued, not that the session rotated — poll check_choreography_job_status for the real outcome. Never report a rotation as done on this result alone.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Validates agent_instance_id/role_name/pickup_text plus the caller's own flow/session context, then writes one AsyncJobManager job row.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: missing_argument: a required field was empty. missing_flow_context: the caller's session_id/flow_id were not resolvable — refused before a job with a hole in it could be created. job_creation_failed: AsyncJobManager.create_job itself failed. async_job_manager_unavailable: the platform's AsyncJobManager is not bound on this solet.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For missing_argument, resolve the ledger agent_instance_id via list_sessions first (never a peer_list/watch id) and confirm the target session's own role_name. missing_flow_context and async_job_manager_unavailable are platform-state issues, not caller mistakes — do not retry the same call unchanged.
